messages:
alex_m: Hey team — hitting weird behavior configuring the Node SDK against our private VPC endpoint behind a corporate proxy. Streaming responses start then hang after ~10s. My client config: ```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  baseURL: 'https://private.redwood.internal',
  apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY,
  timeout: 30000,
  // I'm trying to use a proxy + mTLS via agent
})
``` Any quick ideas? I'm also attaching a client cert via an https.Agent.

maya_dev: Can you paste how you're attaching mTLS? Node's https.Agent needs `cert`/`key`/`ca`. Also corporate proxies often require tunneling (CONNECT). Our JS SDK doesn't implement NTLM tunneling itself — either use `HTTPS_PROXY` env or a tunneling lib (e.g. `tunnel-agent`).

alex_m: I tried `HTTPS_PROXY` but ours is NTLM so env var doesn't auth. I created `new https.Agent({ cert, key, ca, keepAlive: true })` and passed it through `fetchOptions` but streaming still stalls. Logs show `ERR_STREAM_WRITE_AFTER_END` sometimes.

sam_doty: Streaming + retries collide. The SDK's automatic retry wrapper will cancel/replace requests on transient errors which kills streams. If you need uninterrupted streams, disable retries for that call or use the low-level streaming API. Also double-check your baseURL formatting — no trailing slash and host must match cert SAN.

maya_dev: Another gotcha: TLS SNI. If your cert is for `private.redwood.internal` but the proxy rehosts host header, you must set `servername` in the TLS options: ```js
new https.Agent({
  cert, key, ca, keepAlive: true,
  servername: 'private.redwood.internal'
})
``` That fixed the handshake for me when the proxy mangled the Host header.

ops_elena: Also verify VPC egress/NAT rules — we had asymmetric routing where requests to the private control plane went out through the proxy then back in and the proxy closed idle connections after 15s. Setting `keepAlive` + longer socket timeout on proxy helped. If your proxy supports connection upgrade/tunnel, prefer that for streaming.

alex_m: How do I pass the agent into the Redwood client cleanly? README only shows basic `fetchOptions` examples.

maya_dev: You can inject a custom fetch wrapper: ```js
const myFetch = (url, opts) => fetch(url, { ...opts, agent: myAgent })
const client = new RedwoodClient({ baseURL, apiKey, fetch: myFetch })
``` If you're on `undici`, set the global agent or use `undici.Agent`. For axios-style clients, pass `httpAgent`/`httpsAgent` on the request config.

sam_doty: If you want a quick debug path: 1) disable proxy to verify mTLS+streaming works end-to-end; 2) reintroduce proxy but use a simple non-NTLM proxy to isolate auth; 3) reproduce with curl using `--proxy` + `--cert` to see TLS/proxy interplay. Also check SDK retries — streaming calls should opt out: `client.generate({ streaming: true, retries: 0 })` or equivalent.

ci-bot: deploy-bot: Canary for node-sdk 2.3.1 rolled to staging at 2025-10-15T14:20Z :rocket:

alex_m: Thanks — will try keepAlive + SNI + explicit fetch wrapper, and report back with a minimal repro if it still fails.
